title: Confirm UVTT is fundamentally 2D and design how it reconciles with this project's free-3D/discrete-elevation world via the same stacked-layer model already used for procedural generation
objective: Owner correctly observed UVTT is a 2D format. Confirmed precisely: its schema (map_origin/map_size in x/y, line_of_sight as 2D line segments, lights/portals as x/y positions only, the image itself a flat top-down texture) has no height/elevation/3D geometry at all -- inherent to its origin serving classic top-down 2D VTTs. Concretely, this means: imported walls are 2D lines needing extrusion into real 3D wall geometry (assigning a height), imported lights need a Z/height assigned since UVTT only gives x/y, and multi-floor buildings aren't natively represented in one file -- each UVTT file is one flat floor, matching how Foundry's own community 'Levels' module handles multi-story buildings by stacking separate flat Scenes at different simulated elevations. The reconciliation: this project's own procedural generation model already represents buildings as stacked 2D layers extruded vertically (Townscaper-style) and interiors as a per-floor WFC pass (already documented in this same file's 'Interior generation' and 'Terrain elevation' sections) -- structurally the same shape as 'a 2D floor plan plus a rule for turning it into 3D.' Proposing that Tier 2 import populates the exact same per-floor-layer data structure Tier 0/1 procedural generation already produces (wall segments + floor texture + lights + portals, each floor layer assigned a height/Z-offset), rather than building a separate import-specific data model -- directly satisfying this document's own original 'Unifying substrate' principle that all four construction tiers feed the same substrate.
validations: Updated the 'Import (Tier 2): Universal VTT (UVTT)' section's closing paragraph (previously flagged as 'not yet designed') with a concrete reconciliation: UVTT's 2D walls/lights/portals get extruded into 3D (assigned height/Z-offset) using the same per-floor stacked-layer data structure already designed for procedural exterior/interior generation, so imported content and generated content are the same shape once inside the engine -- consistent with the document's own 'Unifying substrate' principle.

Explicitly confirmed, rather than just asserted, why UVTT has no elevation data: its Resolution/line_of_sight/lights/portals fields are all 2D (x/y only), and multi-floor buildings require multiple separate UVTT files (matching Foundry's own community 'Levels' module pattern of stacking flat Scenes at different simulated elevations), not one file with real 3D structure.
No dependency installed, no code written, no ADR reopened -- documentation refinement only, building on findings already recorded, no new external research required for this reconciliation itself.
artifacts: docs/research/vtt-map-and-terrain-construction-options.md (Import (Tier 2) section's closing paragraph replaced with a concrete reconciliation)
